name: Piper PA-44 Seminole
summary: Four-seat light twin with a T-tail, one of the most common multi-engine trainers at US flight schools.

wings: Low, tapered wing from the single-engine Arrow family
engines: Two flat-four engines in compact nacelles
fuselage: Four-seat cabin with a single door on the right and three side windows
tail: T-tail: stabilator mounted on top of a swept fin

tellTales: Small low-wing light twin with a T-tail
Short four-seat cabin with only a right-side door

confusedWith.howToTell: The Seneca has a low tail and a longer six-seat cabin; the Seminole has a T-tail and a short cabin.
The DA42 has very long slender wings, a sleek composite fuselage and a large canopy; the Seminole has a conventional metal cabin with a door and side windows.
The Baron has a conventional low tail; the Seminole has a T-tail.
